jobs.title: ML Research Resident
jobs.description:
Elicit is building a research agent that can use an unlimited amount of test-time compute while keeping its reasoning transparent and verifiable.

The residency

Transformers do a fixed amount of computation per token, and the quality of work degrades rapidly when they are applied iteratively. As research resident, you'll work with us for 3 months on developing computational procedures (operators) that can reliably improve a knowledge state over thousands of iterations.

What is a knowledge state? A knowledge state consists of structured information - for example, a scientific paper might be represented as a set of claims supported by evidence and connected through logical reasoning; this might be combined with scratchpads, evergreen “notes to self”, search trees, and other information.

What counts as improvement? Like scientists, we want LLMs to make genuine progress in understanding - separating inferences from raw evidence, finding connections between ideas, building clearer explanations, and identifying gaps in reasoning. But unlike typical ML systems that are often trained to do “whatever works”, we need improvements that are epistemically sound - each step should make the knowledge state more useful while remaining human-readable. An improvement might reorganize information to better answer a question, find an implicit assumption in an argument, or connect evidence across multiple sources.

As research resident, your work will focus on designing and testing improvement operators that maintain stability over 1000+ iterations while making genuine progress. You'll start with simple cases (e.g., shallow refactoring of scientific papers) and demonstrate reliable iteration before scaling to more complex reasoning tasks.

Developing systems that perform legible reasoning over long horizons addresses core challenges in AI transparency and scalable reasoning.

About You

Strong candidates will have experience with LLMs, good intuitions about what makes reasoning systematic and verifiable, and care about AI transparency.

The best applicants will additionally have a strong software engineering background and concrete examples of how they've applied this background to come up with novel abstractions that push the frontiers of automated reasoning.

Logistics

3-month contract role
Compensation: $12-15k/month depending on experience
Location: In-person (Oakland) or remote (US)
Potential of full-time offer for exceptional candidates

Location and travel

We have a great office in Oakland, CA, and we'd love to see you there if you're local. That said, we're just as happy for you to work remotely. We do get the whole team together for a quarterly retreat somewhere fun, because in-person time matters to us.

Description

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is proud to be the pioneer and recognized leader in Cloud Computing. Our web services provide IT infrastructure used by hundreds of thousands of developers and businesses worldwide, from startups to Global 500 companies across all industries.

jobs.title: AI Research Engineer | World Models
jobs.description:
Machine Learning Engineer | World Models

Location:
Los Altos, CA | On-site / Hybrid
Employment Type:
Full-Time

About Dyssonance

Dyssonance is building a fundamentally different approach to artificial intelligence.

We have developed a physics-inspired approach to intelligence that does not rely on large language models or foundation models as its underlying architecture
. Rather than treating intelligence primarily as a problem of predicting from increasingly large amounts of data, our work focuses on the dynamics of information itself: how an intelligent system forms internal representations of the world, reasons under uncertainty, resolves ambiguity, and continuously updates what it believes as new information arrives.

We are now commercializing this technology as a new category of AI systems: cognitive infrastructure
. Cognitive infrastructure sits beneath applications and agents, providing the underlying capabilities required for persistent state, reasoning, uncertainty, learning, and adaptation. Our goal is not to build another model. It is to build infrastructure for intelligence itself.

Our team brings together former DeepMind, Google, Apple & Amazon researchers and engineers, alongside PhD-level researchers across AI, mathematics, physics, neuroscience, and related fields. We are a small, deeply technical team working across fundamental research, systems engineering, and real-world deployment.

We are looking for an exceptional Machine Learning Engineer focused on World Models
to help develop the internal representations and dynamics that allow intelligent systems to model a changing world.

About the Role

As an AI Research Engineer focused on World Models, you will develop models that allow intelligent systems to learn, maintain, and update internal representations of dynamic and partially observed environments.

You will work closely with our researchers on learned state-space models, latent dynamics, and sequential representations, including recurrent state-space architectures and related approaches.
A central part of the role will be investigating how internal state should be represented, updated, and propagated through time when observations are incomplete, uncertain, or ambiguous, and how those representations can support prediction, inference, reasoning, and planning.

This is not primarily an ML infrastructure role, nor is it a purely theoretical research position.
You should be equally comfortable understanding an architecture mathematically, implementing it in PyTorch or JAX, training it, instrumenting its internal representations, and debugging why it fails.
We are looking for someone who can move from paper to mathematical formulation to implementation to experiment to evidence
quickly and independently.

What You'll Do

Design, implement, and evaluate learned state-space models and latent-dynamics architectures.
Develop and extend SSMs and related approaches for learning representations of dynamic environments.
Explore deterministic, stochastic, discrete, continuous, and hybrid latent-state representations.
Develop mechanisms for latent-state inference and state estimation under partial observability.
Investigate how internal state should be maintained and updated as new, incomplete, uncertain, or contradictory information arrives.
Develop objectives for learning predictive and decision-relevant internal representations.
Investigate architectural choices around recurrence, memory, state abstraction, transition dynamics, and uncertainty.
Study long-horizon latent dynamics, including stability, compounding error, and representational collapse.
Explore how learned world models can support inference, reasoning, planning, and decision-making.
Build rigorous evaluations of predictive accuracy, state quality, generalization, long-horizon consistency, and robustness under distribution shift.
Reproduce, extend, and critically evaluate results from the world-model, state-space modeling, and model-based learning literature.
Translate mathematical and research ideas into rigorous, executable implementations.
Profile and optimize computationally intensive training and inference workloads.
Build tools that shorten the cycle between hypothesis, implementation, experiment, and result.
Collaborate directly with researchers across AI, mathematics, physics, neuroscience, and engineering.
Contribute research prototypes that may ultimately become components of production AI systems.
Maintain high standards for code quality, testing, reproducibility, experimental design, and documentation.

What We're Looking For

Strong engineering ability is essential.

We are not looking for someone who can only propose interesting architectures and hand their implementation to somebody else. You should be capable of independently turning research ideas into working experimental systems.

You likely have:
A MS or PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Mathematics, Physics, Robotics, or another highly quantitative discipline, or equivalent research or engineering experience.
Strong proficiency in Python (at least 3 years of experience) and experience building substantial machine-learning, scientific, or technical software.
Deep experience with PyTorch, JAX, or equivalent modern machine-learning frameworks.
Strong understanding of modern deep learning, including optimization, representation learning, sequence modeling, and latent-variable models.
Experience implementing and training nontrivial neural architectures from research papers.
Strong foundations in probability, linear algebra, optimization, numerical methods, and algorithms.
Experience working with sequential or temporally structured data.
Familiarity with state-space models, sequential latent-variable models, recurrent architectures, or model-based learning.
The ability to read mathematical or theoretical research and translate it into working implementations.
Experience designing experiments capable of validating or falsifying technical hypotheses.
Strong debugging skills across model architecture, training dynamics, numerical computation, data, and experimental infrastructure.
Experience with GPU-based training and performance optimization.
The ability to work autonomously while collaborating closely with a multidisciplinary research team.

Particularly Interesting to Us

We would be especially interested in experience with one or more of:
State-Space Models
Latent dynamics models
Sequential latent-variable models
World-model architectures
Deterministic and stochastic latent representations
Variational inference
Model-based reinforcement learning
Predictive and/or self-supervised representation learning
Long-horizon sequential modeling
Uncertainty estimation
State estimation under partial observability
Generative sequence models
JAX / XLA
PyTorch
GPU-accelerated machine learning
Large-scale model training

Direct experience with every area above is not expected. Deep hands-on experience with learned state-space models or an adjacent class of sequential latent models, strong engineering ability, and the capacity to learn unfamiliar technical domains quickly matter more than breadth across the entire world-model literature.

How We Work

Dyssonance operates differently from a traditional research lab. We care deeply about theoretical understanding, but research must ultimately encounter evidence. We expect researchers and engineers to shorten the distance between an idea and the experiment that can validate or invalidate it. If an experimental loop is too slow, we improve the loop. If infrastructure is blocking an answer, we build better infrastructure. If an assumption can be tested, we test it.

We value people who can challenge an approach rigorously (including their own) and who are comfortable discovering that an elegant idea doesn't work.

A successful Machine Learning Engineer at Dyssonance can encounter an unfamiliar research problem, understand the relevant mathematics and literature, formulate a computational approach, build a credible experiment, and produce evidence that changes what the team believes.

You are the kind of person who reads a paper about a new model architecture and immediately starts thinking about how you would implement it, test it, and determine what it is actually learning.
You are interested in what information an intelligent system needs to preserve in its internal state, how that state should evolve through time, and what happens when observations are incomplete or uncertain.
You enjoy mathematics and first-principles reasoning, but you also love building things.
You can move comfortably between abstraction and implementation.
You don't need a perfectly specified problem before beginning.
You are capable of working independently without becoming intellectually isolated. You actively seek context from the broader system, collaborate with other researchers, and know how to connect your work to the team's larger technical objectives.
And you are excited by problems where the answer may not exist yet.

Why Dyssonance

You'll join a small multidisciplinary technical team of former DeepMind, Google, and Apple researchers and engineers and PhD-level scientists working on fundamental questions about intelligence and computation.

State is central to Dyssonance's approach to intelligence.
We are interested in systems that maintain and revise internal representations of a changing world rather than repeatedly reconstructing one from context.

You'll work directly with the people developing Dyssonance's core AI architecture and have significant ownership over the models, experiments, and systems you build and will have the opportunity to develop world models without being constrained to a predetermined architecture or existing research program. We care about understanding which approaches actually work, why they work, and where they fail.

This is a role for someone who wants to help develop new approaches to how intelligent systems represent and reason about a changing world, not simply scale an established model.

new_jobs.title: ML Research Resident
new_jobs.description:
Elicit is building a research agent that can use an unlimited amount of test-time compute while keeping its reasoning transparent and verifiable.

The residency

Transformers do a fixed amount of computation per token, and the quality of work degrades rapidly when they are applied iteratively. As research resident, you'll work with us for 3 months on developing computational procedures (operators) that can reliably improve a knowledge state over thousands of iterations.

What is a knowledge state? A knowledge state consists of structured information - for example, a scientific paper might be represented as a set of claims supported by evidence and connected through logical reasoning; this might be combined with scratchpads, evergreen “notes to self”, search trees, and other information.

What counts as improvement? Like scientists, we want LLMs to make genuine progress in understanding - separating inferences from raw evidence, finding connections between ideas, building clearer explanations, and identifying gaps in reasoning. But unlike typical ML systems that are often trained to do “whatever works”, we need improvements that are epistemically sound - each step should make the knowledge state more useful while remaining human-readable. An improvement might reorganize information to better answer a question, find an implicit assumption in an argument, or connect evidence across multiple sources.

As research resident, your work will focus on designing and testing improvement operators that maintain stability over 1000+ iterations while making genuine progress. You'll start with simple cases (e.g., shallow refactoring of scientific papers) and demonstrate reliable iteration before scaling to more complex reasoning tasks.

Developing systems that perform legible reasoning over long horizons addresses core challenges in AI transparency and scalable reasoning.

About You

Strong candidates will have experience with LLMs, good intuitions about what makes reasoning systematic and verifiable, and care about AI transparency.

The best applicants will additionally have a strong software engineering background and concrete examples of how they've applied this background to come up with novel abstractions that push the frontiers of automated reasoning.

Machine Learning Engineer | World Models

Location:
Los Altos, CA | On-site / Hybrid

About Dyssonance

Dyssonance is building a fundamentally different approach to artificial intelligence.

We have developed a physics-inspired approach to intelligence that does not rely on large language models or foundation models as its underlying architecture
. Rather than treating intelligence primarily as a problem of predicting from increasingly large amounts of data, our work focuses on the dynamics of information itself: how an intelligent system forms internal representations of the world, reasons under uncertainty, resolves ambiguity, and continuously updates what it believes as new information arrives.

We are now commercializing this technology as a new category of AI systems: cognitive infrastructure
. Cognitive infrastructure sits beneath applications and agents, providing the underlying capabilities required for persistent state, reasoning, uncertainty, learning, and adaptation. Our goal is not to build another model. It is to build infrastructure for intelligence itself.

Our team brings together former DeepMind, Google, Apple & Amazon researchers and engineers, alongside PhD-level researchers across AI, mathematics, physics, neuroscience, and related fields. We are a small, deeply technical team working across fundamental research, systems engineering, and real-world deployment.

We are looking for an exceptional Machine Learning Engineer focused on World Models
to help develop the internal representations and dynamics that allow intelligent systems to model a changing world.

About the Role

As an AI Research Engineer focused on World Models, you will develop models that allow intelligent systems to learn, maintain, and update internal representations of dynamic and partially observed environments.

You will work closely with our researchers on learned state-space models, latent dynamics, and sequential representations, including recurrent state-space architectures and related approaches.
A central part of the role will be investigating how internal state should be represented, updated, and propagated through time when observations are incomplete, uncertain, or ambiguous, and how those representations can support prediction, inference, reasoning, and planning.

This is not primarily an ML infrastructure role, nor is it a purely theoretical research position.
You should be equally comfortable understanding an architecture mathematically, implementing it in PyTorch or JAX, training it, instrumenting its internal representations, and debugging why it fails.
We are looking for someone who can move from paper to mathematical formulation to implementation to experiment to evidence
quickly and independently.

What You'll Do

Design, implement, and evaluate learned state-space models and latent-dynamics architectures.
Develop and extend SSMs and related approaches for learning representations of dynamic environments.
Explore deterministic, stochastic, discrete, continuous, and hybrid latent-state representations.
Develop mechanisms for latent-state inference and state estimation under partial observability.
Investigate how internal state should be maintained and updated as new, incomplete, uncertain, or contradictory information arrives.
Develop objectives for learning predictive and decision-relevant internal representations.
Investigate architectural choices around recurrence, memory, state abstraction, transition dynamics, and uncertainty.
Study long-horizon latent dynamics, including stability, compounding error, and representational collapse.
Explore how learned world models can support inference, reasoning, planning, and decision-making.
Build rigorous evaluations of predictive accuracy, state quality, generalization, long-horizon consistency, and robustness under distribution shift.
Reproduce, extend, and critically evaluate results from the world-model, state-space modeling, and model-based learning literature.
Translate mathematical and research ideas into rigorous, executable implementations.
Profile and optimize computationally intensive training and inference workloads.
Build tools that shorten the cycle between hypothesis, implementation, experiment, and result.
Collaborate directly with researchers across AI, mathematics, physics, neuroscience, and engineering.
Contribute research prototypes that may ultimately become components of production AI systems.
Maintain high standards for code quality, testing, reproducibility, experimental design, and documentation.

What We're Looking For

Strong engineering ability is essential.

We are not looking for someone who can only propose interesting architectures and hand their implementation to somebody else. You should be capable of independently turning research ideas into working experimental systems.

You likely have:
A MS or PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Mathematics, Physics, Robotics, or another highly quantitative discipline, or equivalent research or engineering experience.
Strong proficiency in Python (at least 3 years of experience) and experience building substantial machine-learning, scientific, or technical software.
Deep experience with PyTorch, JAX, or equivalent modern machine-learning frameworks.
Strong understanding of modern deep learning, including optimization, representation learning, sequence modeling, and latent-variable models.
Experience implementing and training nontrivial neural architectures from research papers.
Strong foundations in probability, linear algebra, optimization, numerical methods, and algorithms.
Experience working with sequential or temporally structured data.
Familiarity with state-space models, sequential latent-variable models, recurrent architectures, or model-based learning.
The ability to read mathematical or theoretical research and translate it into working implementations.
Experience designing experiments capable of validating or falsifying technical hypotheses.
Strong debugging skills across model architecture, training dynamics, numerical computation, data, and experimental infrastructure.
Experience with GPU-based training and performance optimization.
The ability to work autonomously while collaborating closely with a multidisciplinary research team.

Particularly Interesting to Us

We would be especially interested in experience with one or more of:
State-Space Models
Latent dynamics models
Sequential latent-variable models
World-model architectures
Deterministic and stochastic latent representations
Variational inference
Model-based reinforcement learning
Predictive and/or self-supervised representation learning
Long-horizon sequential modeling
Uncertainty estimation
State estimation under partial observability
Generative sequence models
JAX / XLA
PyTorch
GPU-accelerated machine learning
Large-scale model training

Direct experience with every area above is not expected. Deep hands-on experience with learned state-space models or an adjacent class of sequential latent models, strong engineering ability, and the capacity to learn unfamiliar technical domains quickly matter more than breadth across the entire world-model literature.

How We Work

Dyssonance operates differently from a traditional research lab. We care deeply about theoretical understanding, but research must ultimately encounter evidence. We expect researchers and engineers to shorten the distance between an idea and the experiment that can validate or invalidate it. If an experimental loop is too slow, we improve the loop. If infrastructure is blocking an answer, we build better infrastructure. If an assumption can be tested, we test it.

We value people who can challenge an approach rigorously (including their own) and who are comfortable discovering that an elegant idea doesn't work.

A successful Machine Learning Engineer at Dyssonance can encounter an unfamiliar research problem, understand the relevant mathematics and literature, formulate a computational approach, build a credible experiment, and produce evidence that changes what the team believes.

You Might Be a Great Fit If

You are the kind of person who reads a paper about a new model architecture and immediately starts thinking about how you would implement it, test it, and determine what it is actually learning.
You are interested in what information an intelligent system needs to preserve in its internal state, how that state should evolve through time, and what happens when observations are incomplete or uncertain.
You enjoy mathematics and first-principles reasoning, but you also love building things.
You can move comfortably between abstraction and implementation.
You don't need a perfectly specified problem before beginning.
You are capable of working independently without becoming intellectually isolated. You actively seek context from the broader system, collaborate with other researchers, and know how to connect your work to the team's larger technical objectives.
And you are excited by problems where the answer may not exist yet.

Why Dyssonance

You'll join a small multidisciplinary technical team of former DeepMind, Google, and Apple researchers and engineers and PhD-level scientists working on fundamental questions about intelligence and computation.

State is central to Dyssonance's approach to intelligence.
We are interested in systems that maintain and revise internal representations of a changing world rather than repeatedly reconstructing one from context.

You'll work directly with the people developing Dyssonance's core AI architecture and have significant ownership over the models, experiments, and systems you build and will have the opportunity to develop world models without being constrained to a predetermined architecture or existing research program. We care about understanding which approaches actually work, why they work, and where they fail.

This is a role for someone who wants to help develop new approaches to how intelligent systems represent and reason about a changing world, not simply scale an established model.

Responsibilities

About the Team&Role

Seed Model–Alignment & Preparedness is dedicated to advancing AI safety alongside frontier model capabilities. Backed by sustained investment and substantial compute resources, we tackle fundamental challenges in alignment, safety evaluation, and preparedness for emerging risks—translating research into safe, reliable AI systems that benefit people.

We’re looking for researchers to make frontier models and agents safer, with a strong focus on agent RL: training agents that stay safe and controllable in tool use, code execution, and long-horizon tasks.

We are looking for talented individuals to join our team. As a graduate, you will get opportunities to pursue bold ideas, tackle complex challenges, and unlock limitless growth.

Successful candidates must be able to commit to an onboarding date by the end of the year. Please state your availability and graduation date clearly in your resume.

Responsibilities

Agent RL & safety training: Use RL, SFT, and preference optimization to train agents safely. Design environments, rewards, and training data that reduce deception, reward hacking, and unauthorized actions, and teach agents to check authorization, recognize risks, and stop when needed, without sacrificing useful autonomy. Ensure safety generalizes to new tasks and holds up through further training.
Frontier risk assessment: Partner with domain experts to evaluate dangerous capabilities (e.g., CBRN, cybersecurity), model threats, and build safeguards. Provide empirical evidence to guide development and deployment decisions.
Automated red teaming: Build automated attack generation and adversarial training methods to harden models against jailbreaks, prompt injection, and other adversarial inputs.
Monitoring & oversight: Detect risks from inputs and outputs, execution traces, chains of thought, and internal representations. Build oversight models, action review, and permission controls, and measure their effectiveness, evasion resistance, and cost.
Failure analysis & deployment: Turn real-world failures into reproducible experiments and pinpoint root causes through controlled studies and ablations. Work with pre-training, post-training, infra, and product teams to ship what works at scale.

Experience with agent RL, including environment design, reward design for multi-step tasks, and long-horizon or multi-agent training.
